about.p1: Pheidon was king of Argos in the 7th century BC, one of the most powerful rulers of his time in the Peloponnese.
about.p2: He is credited with the first system of weights and measures in the Greek world, and by some accounts the first coinage.
about.p3: His name is linked to the verb pheidomai: to spare, to economise. The Greek word pheido, meaning thrift, shares the same root.

dashboard.title: Overview

overspend.title: Overspending on {{category}}
overspend.plain: This month you spent {{overspend}} more on {{category}} ({{current}} against an average of {{average}}).
overspend.withDonor: This month you spent {{overspend}} more on {{category}}. To stay within budget, consider cutting {{donorCut}} from {{donorCategory}}.

cashflow.body: The month closes at {{net}}, a {{savingsPercent}}% savings rate. A healthy target is {{targetPercent}}%.

win.title: Good result on {{category}}
win.body: You spent {{saved}} less than your average, {{deviationPercent}}% below. Keep it up and the yearly goal gets closer.

goal.withCuts: You need {{required}} per month and {{projected}} is projected. That leaves {{gap}} short each month, which the cuts below cover ({{cutsCover}}).
goal.deficit: With your declared income the forecast runs a deficit of {{projected}} per month: nothing will accumulate, you'll be spending what you already have. Before discussing the goal, you need either {{extraIncome}} more income per month or a cut in fixed costs. Available cuts in flexible categories only reach {{cutsCover}}.
goal.alternatives: By the target date {{achievable}} is projected, leaving {{totalGap}} short. Even maximum cuts don't close it. Realistically you have three options: push the goal back {{extraMonths}} months, reduce the amount to {{achievable}}, or find {{extraIncome}} extra income per month.

cliff.title: Income drops from {{month}}
cliff.body: When "{{label}}" ends, monthly income goes from {{before}} to {{after}}, that's {{drop}} less. Plans already account for this drop.

income.title: Expected income
income.label: Description

allowance.title: Free to spend
allowance.perDay: {{amount}} per day for the remaining {{days}} days
allowance.impossible: With your current income nothing is left for discretionary spending: fixed costs, essentials and the goal contribution use it all. You need either a smaller goal or more income.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.needData: Add a few entries first. There is nothing to analyse without data.
analysis.notEnoughMonths: You have {{have}} months of data. From {{need}} onwards, comparisons against an average become reliable. Until then the figures are correct, but the trends are noise.
analysis.adviceNote: The statistics above are computed locally and are exact. The suggestions are an interpretation of those same figures.
analysis.nothingToSay: Nothing noteworthy came up this time.
analysis.sourceLlm: The suggestions were written by a language model, on top of statistics computed locally. The model does no arithmetic.
analysis.sourceRules: The suggestions came from the local rules. The language model is not enabled or did not respond.
analysis.adviceNoteLocal: The statistics above are computed locally and are exact. The suggestions come from local rules applied to those same figures.

settings.bufferHint: A share of monthly income set aside and excluded from your free-to-spend limit. It absorbs the unexpected: a tyre, a doctor, a gift you did not see coming. At 0% your limit rises, but any unplanned expense puts you over.
